summary:
American Samoa's criminal law does not punish consensual sodomy. The 1979 revision of the criminal law, which took effect in 1980, retained prohibition only for public acts, prostitution, conduct involving minors and persons unable to consent. The first sodomy statute, enacted in 1963, criminalised male homosexual and heterosexual conduct and did not address lesbian sex. The age of consent is 16, regardless of gender or sexual orientation.

Same-sex marriage is not licensed in American Samoa. In July 2015 Attorney General Talauega Eleasalo Ale was reviewing whether the United States Supreme Court's marriage-equality ruling applied to the territory, and the Governor stated at the time that it did not, citing the territory's preamble, its constitution, Christian values and its unorganised and unincorporated political status. No same-sex couple had filed an application for a marriage licence then, and none has applied to date.

A 2026 law review article by two attorneys practising in American Samoa concludes that the 2015 ruling does apply despite those official statements, and that the territory would have to issue a marriage certificate to any same-sex couple that applied. The article sets out the litigation route: the High Court of American Samoa first, with the Territorial Registrar as defendant, then the United States Department of the Interior. Reporting from the territory in July 2024 described the local ban as still treated as operative on the island and its durability under the Fourteenth Amendment as an open question, with a survey by a constitutional and comparative law professor testing the issue.

Birth certificates in American Samoa are altered only to correct information that was erroneous at the time of recordation or to reflect a name change due to adoption, under a High Court ruling that the Office of Vital Statistics applies to applications from transgender individuals. The office changes the name on a birth certificate when presented with a name change order, and may change the gender marker with medical documentation of the sex change.

Protection machinery has been used locally. In September 2023 the United States Justice Department secured a settlement with the American Samoa Government resolving an employment-discrimination case involving harassment of a transgender employee, following a June 2023 federal civil action that cited a hostile work environment in a transgender woman's lawsuit against the territorial government over her gender identity. In February 2023 a 51-year-old man was charged with sexual abuse of a 16-year-old transgender teen.

American Samoan society is highly religious, and conservative attitudes on gender and sexuality tend to dominate. Reserved public behaviour is expected of people of all orientations, and open displays of affection between couples, same-sex or opposite-sex, may offend. Against that, fa'afafine, boys raised as girls to take an important domestic role in Samoan communal life, are described in the sources as a recognised and integral part of traditional Samoan culture, and the territory is described as tolerant and accepting of transgender people and identities.
tangentialFactors:
The Fono Senate rejected a bill on 20 March 2003 that would have outlawed same-sex marriage, after the House Judiciary Committee recommended it be killed. The sponsor, Representative Sua Carl Schuster, sought to preempt the marriage litigation then unfolding in United States states. At the committee hearing fa'afafine resident Tifanny Poutasi testified that Samoan fa'afafine do not seek marriage with other men, describing them as men expressing femininity through dress and speech and citing Christian upbringing. The territory therefore declined to enact a formal marriage ban before the 2015 ruling, and the hearing record preserves contemporaneous local fa'afafine views on the question.

In January 2016 the American Samoa Senate unanimously confirmed former Attorney General Fiti Alexander Sunia as a District Court judge after he told the confirmation hearing that he had not read the 2015 Supreme Court decision, that the district court does not deal with it, and that he would not perform weddings for same-sex couples unless local laws change. Eighteen months after the ruling, the territory's judiciary was operating on the premise that it did not automatically apply.

The sources describe American Samoa as the only United States jurisdiction, alongside certain tribal jurisdictions, still enforcing a ban on same-sex couples marrying. A 2009 travel column set the territory apart from a neighbouring Pacific island nation it characterised as marked by homophobia, describing homosexuality as widely accepted in Samoan culture while noting that reserved behaviour is expected of people of all orientations; the same column reported roughly 57,000 residents across seven islands and atolls and hotels geared to business travel in Pago Pago.

The American Samoa Code does not specify the sex of the parties to a marriage but refers to the age of "the male" and "the female" and prescribes a form in which parties identify as "son" and as "daughter".
localsOnly:
The Society of Fa'afafine in American Samoa (SOFIAS) was formed in 2010 by merging the American Samoa Island Queens Association and the American 7s Association, is re-anchored explicitly to cultural pride, runs annual events and campaigns for the fa'afafine community, and defines fa'afafine as born male but embodying both male and female traits and as a recognised and integral part of traditional Samoan culture. The first Pride festival was held in August 2016 in Utulei with pageant, song, dance and poetry competitions. Beauty pageants among the fa'afafine community are popular and families generally attend in numbers.

Residents seeking to correct a birth certificate must proceed through the Office of Vital Statistics, which changes the name when presented with a name change order and may change the gender marker with medical documentation of the sex change; amendments to reflect a change of sex recorded after birth are refused under the High Court ruling, which limits alterations to errors present at recordation or to name changes on adoption.

Employment protection has been enforced against the territorial government itself: the September 2023 settlement with the United States Justice Department resolved an employment-discrimination case involving harassment of a transgender employee, and the June 2023 federal civil action had cited a hostile work environment in a transgender woman's lawsuit against the American Samoa Government over her gender identity.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether the 2015 marriage-equality ruling is operative in American Samoa is unresolved. Official statements from 2015 and on-island reporting from July 2024 treat the local ban as operative and its constitutional durability as an open question, while the 2026 law review article concludes the ruling applies and that a certificate would have to be issued; no court in the territory has decided the point, and no same-sex couple has applied for a licence.

No sourced material documents hate-crime provisions covering gender identity in the territory, their charging practice, or their enforcement. The February 2023 sexual-abuse charge is a single documented incident and no denominator-based figure for violence against transgender people in American Samoa appears in the sources.

Access to gender-affirming care, prison or detention placement rules by gender, and airport screening treatment specific to gender-nonconforming travellers in the territory are not sourced here. How the territory's birth-certificate gender-marker rule interacts with federal passport policy for residents is likewise not addressed by the sources.

The 2009 travel column's characterisations of local acceptance are descriptive and dated, and carry no legal force.
